title: Space and Astronomy
description: Look up at the stars and travel far.

entries.title: The Solar System
entries.summary: Our Sun has eight planets going around it.
entries.introduction: Have you ever wondered how many planets are near us?
entries.curiosityQuestion: If you could visit one planet, which would you choose and why?

grade1.body: The Sun is at the centre and eight planets travel around it. From closest to farthest they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Between them are lots of moons, asteroids and comets.

grade2.body: The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system. Eight planets travel around the Sun in paths called orbits. From closest to farthest they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The four inner planets are made of rock. The four outer planets are much bigger and mostly made of gas. Between the planets are moons, asteroids and comets.

sections.title: The Sun and planets
paragraphs: The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system.
Eight planets travel around the Sun.
The planets move in paths called orbits.
From closest to farthest: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

facts.title: Huge Sun
facts.text: The Sun is 109 times wider than the Earth.

facts.title: One year
facts.text: It takes Earth 365 days to go around the Sun.

sections.title: Space in real life
examples: Seeing the Moon and stars in the night sky.
Watching a rocket launch on television.

vocabulary.definition: The Sun and all the planets that travel around it.
The path a planet follows as it travels around the Sun.
A big ball of rock or gas that travels around a star.
A rocky object that travels around the Sun, smaller than a planet.

activity.title: Pace out the solar system
activity.description: Use steps to show how far apart the planets are from the Sun.
steps: Place one marker for the Sun.
Take steps to place each planet marker at the right distance.
Walk from the Sun to each planet and back.

sections.title: Something to wonder about
sections.curiosity: What do you think it would be like to stand on another planet?

entries.title: The Moon
entries.summary: The Moon is Earth's neighbour in space.
entries.body: The Moon goes around the Earth about once a month. The Moon has no air and no water, and its surface is covered in craters made by ancient impacts. People have walked on the Moon and left footprints there.
facts: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no wind.
Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.
The Moon is about a quarter the width of the Earth.

entries.title: The Planets
entries.body: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. Jupiter is the biggest and has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot. Saturn has beautiful rings made of ice and rock. Neptune is the coldest and windiest planet.
facts: Four planets are called rocky planets.
Venus is the hottest planet because its thick blanket of gas holds heat.

entries.title: Astronauts
entries.summary: Astronauts are people who go into space.
entries.body: Astronauts wear a spacesuit that gives them air and keeps them safe. Inside a spacecraft they can float because there is no pull towards the floor. Astronauts on the International Space Station do science and look down at the Earth.
facts: The Space Station goes around the Earth about every 90 minutes.
Astronauts grow a little taller in space.
There have been more than 300 people from about 20 countries.

entries.title: Stars
entries.summary: Stars are huge balls of hot gas that make their own light.
entries.body: The Sun is the closest star to us. Stars look tiny because they are very far away, but many of them are much bigger than the Sun. A group of stars that looks like a shape in the sky is called a constellation.
facts: The Sun is about 93 million miles away.
Red stars are cooler than blue stars.
Shooting stars are really meteors - bits of space rock burning up.

entries.title: The First Moon Landing
entries.summary: People walked on the Moon in 1969.
entries.body: On 20 July 1969 the Apollo 11 spacecraft landed on the Moon. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin stepped out and left footprints that are still there today, because there is no wind to blow them away.
facts: The footprints will stay on the Moon for millions of years.
Six people have walked on the Moon.
The mission took about eight days to reach the Moon.

questions.prompt: How many planets go around our Sun?
questions.explanation: There are eight planets in our solar system.
Jupiter is the biggest planet and has a giant storm on it.
Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.

questions.prompt: The Moon has air and wind like Earth.
questions.explanation: The Moon has no air, so there is no wind or weather at all.

questions.prompt: What is a group of stars in the sky called?
questions.explanation: A constellation is a pattern of stars, like the Big Dipper.

questions.prompt: In what year did people first walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.prompt: Why do astronauts float inside a spacecraft?
options: There is no pull towards the floor
The room is full of air
questions.explanation: In orbit everything is in free fall, so they float.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

questions.prompt: The footprints on the Moon have been blown away by wind.
questions.explanation: There is no wind on the Moon, so the footprints are still there.

questions.prompt: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is our nearest star.
